Build a stress spec from an ADaM basic data structure

Source: R/constructors.R
stress_spec_adam.Rd

Subsets a CDISC ADaM BDS data set (ADEFF, ADQS and the like) to one parameter, the analysis-flagged post-baseline records, orders the visits by their numeric code and builds the spec with the baseline value as a covariate by default.

Usage

stress_spec_adam(
  bds,
  paramcd,
  response = "CHG",
  subject = "USUBJID",
  visit = "AVISIT",
  visitn = "AVISITN",
  treatment = "TRTP",
  reference = NULL,
  active = NULL,
  covariates = ~BASE,
  contrast_visit = NULL,
  analysis_flag = "ANL01FL",
  drop_baseline = TRUE,
  filter = NULL,
  covariance = "us",
  method = "Kenward-Roger",
  vcov = "Kenward-Roger-Linear",
  alpha = 0.05,
  weights = "equal",
  label = paste(paramcd, response)
)

Arguments

bds

A BDS data frame.

paramcd

The PARAMCD value to analyse.

response

Response column, usually "CHG" or "PCHG".

subject, visit, visitn, treatment

Column names (USUBJID, AVISIT, AVISITN, TRTP by default).

reference, active, contrast_visit, covariance, method, vcov, alpha, weights, label

As in stress_spec().

covariates

Covariates; the default is the baseline value BASE.

analysis_flag

Name of a flag column kept where equal to "Y"; NULL keeps all records.

drop_baseline

Drop records flagged ABLFL == "Y" or with a non-positive visitn.

filter

Optional function of the data returning the rows to keep, applied after the other subsets (an analysis-phase restriction, say).

Value

A stress_spec.

Examples

bds <- transform(mmrm::fev_data, PARAMCD = "FEV1", CHG = FEV1 - FEV1_BL, BASE = FEV1_BL,
                 AVISITN = VISITN, TRTP = ARMCD, ANL01FL = "Y")
stress_spec_adam(bds, "FEV1", response = "CHG", visit = "AVISIT", reference = "PBO")
#> <stress_spec> FEV1 CHG
#>   data:       800 rows, 200 subjects, visits VIS1 VIS2 VIS3 VIS4
#>   model:      CHG ~ BASE + TRTP + AVISIT + TRTP:AVISIT + us(AVISIT | USUBJID)
#>   contrast:   TRT - PBO at VIS4
#>   inference:  Kenward-Roger df, Kenward-Roger-Linear vcov, alpha 0.05
